spans.s:
Meṣa denotes ‘ram’ in the Rigveda^1 and later,^2 while Meṣī
means ‘sheep.’^3 Both words are also used to denote the
[]
‘wool’^4 of the sheep, especially as employed for the Soma
filter. A wild (āraṇya) ram is mentioned in the Vājasaneyi
Saṃhitā.^5
1) i. 43, 6; 116, 16; viii. 2, 40; x. 27,
17, etc.
2) Av. vi. 49, 2; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā,
iii. 59; xix. 90; xxiv. 30; Taittirīya
Saṃhitā, vii. 4, 12, 1; Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāh-
maṇa, i. 1; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, iii. 3,
4, 18, etc.
3) Rv. i. 43, 6; Vājasaneyī Saṃhitā,
iii. 59; xxiv. 1; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa,
i. 6, 4, 4. etc.
4) Meṣa, Rv. viii. 86, 11; Meṣī. ix. 8, 5;
86, 47; 107, 11.
5) xxiv. 30.
Cf. Hopkins, Journal of the American
Oriental Society, 17, 66, 67.
